name: European Statistics Regulation
objectives: Establishes a legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of European statistics. It sets statistical principles such as professional independence, impartiality, reliability and statistical confidentiality, defines the European Statistical System of Eurostat and national statistical authorities, and governs the European statistical programme, data access and the protection of confidential data.
source: Arts. 1-2 and recitals 1-6 of the act

name: Digital Europe Programme
objectives: Funds the digital transformation of Europe's economy, industry and society for 2021-2027, aiming to improve EU competitiveness, bridge the digital divide and reinforce strategic autonomy. It supports deployment in five areas: high performance computing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and trust, advanced digital skills, and the best use of digital capacities and interoperability, including through European Digital Innovation Hubs. Its budget is EUR 7.588 billion.

name: InvestEU Programme
objectives: Supports EU policy objectives by mobilising public and private investment through an EU budget guarantee for financing and investment operations by implementing partners such as the EIB Group. It covers four policy windows: sustainable infrastructure; research, innovation and digitisation; SMEs; and social investment and skills. It also creates an advisory hub and an investment portal. The EU guarantee for its EU compartment is about EUR 26.2 billion.

name: Connecting Europe Facility
objectives: Funds the building, development and modernisation of trans-European networks in transport, energy and digital sectors for 2021-2027, and facilitates cross-border cooperation on renewable energy. In the digital sector it supports projects such as very high capacity backbone networks, 5G systems along transport corridors and the digitalisation of transport and energy networks. Its financial envelope is EUR 33.71 billion.

name: Horizon Europe
objectives: Establishes the EU framework programme for research and innovation for 2021-2027 and its rules for participation and dissemination. It aims to strengthen the Union's scientific and technological bases, foster competitiveness, tackle global challenges and strengthen the European Research Area. It funds excellent science, collaborative research on global challenges and industrial competitiveness, and innovation through the European Innovation Council, with EUR 86.123 billion for its main specific programme and the EIT.

name: Single Market Programme
objectives: Funds actions for 2021-2027 to improve the functioning of the internal market and to produce high-quality European statistics. It supports enforcement of EU law, market access and competitiveness for SMEs, European standardisation, consumer protection, and food, animal and plant health, and strengthens cooperation between national authorities and the Commission. Its financial envelope is EUR 4.208 billion.

name: European Cybersecurity Competence Centre
objectives: Establishes the European Cybersecurity Industrial, Technology and Research Competence Centre, a Network of National Coordination Centres and a Cybersecurity Competence Community. It aims to strengthen the EU's cybersecurity capacities, technological sovereignty and industrial competitiveness. The Centre sets strategic priorities for research, innovation and deployment and manages cybersecurity funding under the Digital Europe Programme and Horizon Europe.
source: Arts 1, 3-5 and recitals 1-10 of the act

name: Recovery and Resilience Facility
objectives: Establishes a temporary facility to help Member States recover from the COVID-19 crisis and become more resilient, supporting the green and digital transitions. It funds reforms and investments set out in national recovery and resilience plans, released when agreed milestones and targets are met; plans must devote at least 20% to digital objectives. It provides up to EUR 312.5 billion in grants and EUR 360 billion in loans (2018 prices).

name: EuroHPC Joint Undertaking Regulation
objectives: Establishes the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking, based in Luxembourg, as a partnership between the Union, participating states and private members. Its mission is to develop, deploy and maintain a world-class federated supercomputing, quantum computing and data infrastructure in the EU, support research and innovation in the technologies involved, and widen access for public and private users. The Union contribution is up to EUR 3.0813 billion.

name: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
objectives: Sets up nine joint undertakings: public-private partnerships that carry out research and innovation under Horizon Europe in areas such as key digital technologies, smart networks and services, clean aviation, rail, hydrogen, health and bio-based industries. It sets out each partnership's objectives and tasks, membership, organisation and operating rules, including the contributions of the EU and of private and public members.

name: Digitalisation of judicial cooperation Regulation
objectives: Creates a uniform legal framework for electronic communication between courts and other competent authorities in cross-border judicial cooperation in civil, commercial and criminal matters. It also allows people and businesses to communicate electronically with authorities in cross-border civil and commercial cases. It sets rules on hearings by videoconference, electronic signatures and seals, the legal effect of electronic documents and electronic payment of fees.

name: Union Secure Connectivity Programme
objectives: Establishes a programme to provide secure satellite communication services to government-authorised users in the EU through a multi-orbital connectivity system under civil control (known as IRIS²). It also aims to enable commercial services, including high-speed broadband, and to reduce communication dead zones. It sets the programme's objectives, funding rules and implementation, with a budget of EUR 1.65 billion for 2023-2027.

name: Cybersecurity Regulation (EU institutions)
objectives: Aims to achieve a high common level of cybersecurity within EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. It requires each of them to set up an internal cybersecurity risk-management, governance and control framework and sets rules on risk management, incident reporting and information sharing. It establishes an Interinstitutional Cybersecurity Board and sets out the role of CERT-EU, the EU entities' cybersecurity service.

name: Information Security Regulation
objectives: Would lay down common information security rules for all EU institutions and bodies. It would apply to all information they handle and store, both non-classified and EU classified information, with common confidentiality levels and protective measures. It would create an Interinstitutional Coordination Group of the institutions' security authorities to issue guidance and work with Member States' national security authorities.
source: Arts. 1-2 and recitals 2 and 8 of the proposal; explanatory memorandum

name: Single Market Emergency Instrument (IMERA)
objectives: Creates a framework to anticipate, prepare for and respond to the impact of crises on the EU internal market. It aims to keep goods, services and people moving freely and to ensure the availability of crisis-relevant goods and services. It sets up an Internal Market Emergency and Resilience Board, contingency planning and measures for vigilance and emergency modes, including joint public procurement.

name: Interoperable Europe Act
objectives: Aims to make public administrations' digital services work together across borders. Applies to EU bodies and public sector bodies that regulate, provide or manage trans-European digital public services. It requires interoperability assessments before binding requirements are set, creates an Interoperable Europe Board and portal to steer and share reusable solutions, and supports innovation measures such as regulatory sandboxes.
source: Art. 1 and recitals 35, 49-51, 101 of the act

name: Critical Raw Materials Act
objectives: Aims to secure the EU's access to a secure, resilient and sustainable supply of critical raw materials. It identifies critical and strategic raw materials, sets benchmarks for EU extraction, processing and recycling capacity, supports 'strategic projects' with faster permitting and access to finance, requires monitoring and stress tests of supply risks, and promotes circularity and the free movement of these materials in the internal market.
source: Art. 1 and recitals of the act

name: Net-Zero Industry Act
objectives: Aims to secure the EU's supply of net-zero technologies by scaling up their manufacturing in Europe, in support of climate neutrality, quality jobs and competitiveness. It supports manufacturing projects with faster permitting and 'strategic project' status, creates an EU market for CO2 storage, encourages demand through sustainability and resilience criteria in public procurement and auctions, and promotes skills academies and regulatory sandboxes.
source: Art. 1 and recitals of the act

name: Cyber Solidarity Act
objectives: Aims to strengthen the EU's capacity to detect, prepare for and respond to significant and large-scale cyber threats and incidents. It establishes a European Cybersecurity Alert System of cross-border cyber hubs, a Cybersecurity Emergency Mechanism to help Member States prepare and respond, including through an EU Cybersecurity Reserve of trusted private providers, and an Incident Review Mechanism to assess major incidents.
source: Art. 1 and recitals of the act

name: Compulsory licensing of patents Regulation
objectives: Aims to ensure access to crisis-relevant products during a crisis or emergency declared under an EU crisis mechanism. It creates a Union compulsory licence, granted by the Commission as a measure of last resort and in the public interest, that allows the use of patents, utility models and supplementary protection certificates without the holder's consent, subject to conditions and remuneration of the rights holder.
source: Art. 1-2 and recitals of the act

name: Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform (STEP)
objectives: Establishes a platform to support the development and manufacturing of critical technologies in the digital, clean and biotech sectors and in defence, and their value chains. It channels funding from existing EU programmes, adds EUR 1.5 billion to the European Defence Fund envelope for STEP objectives, awards a 'Sovereignty Seal' to quality projects and creates a Sovereignty Portal listing funding opportunities.

name: EU Digital Travel Application Regulation
objectives: Would create an EU Digital Travel application allowing travellers to create digital travel credentials from their passports or identity cards, enter travel data, and submit them securely in advance to border authorities. It aims to facilitate travel and border checks at the Schengen external borders and sets the conditions for developing, operating and maintaining the application.

name: Interoperability of EU information systems (borders and visa) Regulation
objectives: Establishes a framework to make EU information systems for borders, visas and migration, such as the Entry/Exit System, VIS, ETIAS and SIS, work together. It creates a European search portal, a shared biometric matching service, a common identity repository and a multiple-identity detector, and sets data quality rules and conditions for access by authorities and Europol.
